posts.title: Parking, travel and kit fees on a freelance AV invoice
posts.description: Freelance AV invoice expenses: how to bill parking, mileage and your kit fee as separate lines, and how to word them so they get approved.
posts.imageAlt: Parking, travel and kit fees on a freelance AV invoice

faq.q: Should I mark up expenses on a freelance invoice?
faq.a: Only if you agreed to it before the job. The usual practice for pass-through costs like parking, tolls and parts is to bill them at cost with a receipt.

faq.q: Can I charge a kit fee on top of my day rate?
faq.a: Only if you told the company your day rate didn't include your kit. If your quoted rate already covers your gear, adding a kit fee on top is double billing.

faq.q: How should I bill mileage as a freelance AV tech?
faq.a: Use a per-mile rate you stated before the job, show the miles and the rate on the invoice, and say where you start from. The IRS standard mileage rate is a common reference point.

faq.q: Do I need receipts for small expenses?
faq.a: Attach one for every pass-through cost, even parking. It's what lets accounts payable approve the line without a back-and-forth.

posts.title: Setting day rates for AV rental gear
posts.description: How to set a day rate for AV rental gear you own: work from payback and real utilization, then check it against your market.
posts.imageAlt: Setting day rates for AV rental gear

faq.q: How do I set a day rate for AV equipment I own?
faq.a: Add up the full cost of the item and its accessories, choose a target return and useful life, estimate how many days a year it will realistically rent, and divide. Then compare the result with what other rental houses in your market charge.

faq.q: Is there a standard percentage of purchase price for a day rate?
faq.a: No. Percentage rules of thumb exist, but they ignore utilization and lifespan. Use them only as a quick sanity check on the number you calculate.

faq.q: How often should I update my rental rates?
faq.a: Review them once or twice a year against your actual days out, repair costs and what the market is charging, and update the items that have drifted.

posts.title: How to price an AV installation by room
posts.description: Price an AV installation room by room: scope the space, split equipment, materials, labor and programming, add contingency, and set change-order rules.
posts.imageAlt: How to price an AV installation by room

faq.q: Should I charge for the site visit?
faq.a: Many installers do, and credit it against the project if the client signs. Whatever you choose, state it in writing before you go.

faq.q: How much contingency should I add?
faq.a: There is no standard figure. Use a percentage you can defend from your own past jobs, and show it as its own line so the client sees it is deliberate.

faq.q: Should I give one price per room or an itemized quote?
faq.a: Give both: an itemized breakdown for the technical reader and a room total for whoever signs. The itemized version also protects you when scope changes.

faq.q: Can I reuse a quote from a similar room?
faq.a: Yes, as a starting point. Copy it, then check the room against your scope list so you do not carry over assumptions that no longer apply.

posts.title: How to invoice an AV company as a freelance tech
posts.description: How to invoice as a freelance AV tech: billing details to get before the gig, what to send after strike, and how to follow up when payment is late.
posts.keyword: how to invoice as a freelance av tech
posts.imageAlt: How to invoice an AV company as a freelance tech

faq.q: Who should I send my invoice to at an AV company?
faq.a: Send it to the billing or accounts payable address the company gives you, and copy the person who booked you. If no one has told you, ask when you're booked.

faq.q: How soon after a gig should I invoice?
faq.a: Within a day or two of strike. Invoices sent while the show is fresh are matched to the crew sheet quickly and approved sooner.

faq.q: Do I need to send a W-9 to every AV company?
faq.a: Send one to each new company you work for as an independent contractor, before or with your first invoice. They need it on file to report what they paid you. Ask your accountant about your own tax situation.

faq.q: What should I do if an AV company pays late?
faq.a: Follow up on the due date with the invoice attached, again a week later with the booker copied, and call if it's still unpaid after two or three weeks. Most late payments are stuck, not disputed.

posts.title: How to calculate overtime for AV crew calls
posts.description: How to calculate AV crew overtime and double time from a day rate, what to agree before the call, and how to quote it so clients aren't surprised.
posts.imageAlt: How to calculate overtime for AV crew calls

faq.q: How do you calculate overtime on a day rate?
faq.a: Divide the day rate by the number of hours it covers to get the hourly base. Overtime hours are paid at 1.5 times that base and double-time hours at 2 times. A $600 day covering 10 hours gives $90 an hour for overtime and $120 for double time.

faq.q: When does overtime start for AV crew?
faq.a: For freelancers, when your agreement says it does, often after the hours the day rate covers. For employees, the law sets the minimum: after 40 hours a week federally, and in some states, such as California, also after 8 hours in a day.

faq.q: What is double time for AV crew?
faq.a: Double time is pay at 2 times the hourly base for very long days. When it starts is set by your crew rules; 12 hours is a common threshold. California requires it for non-exempt employees after 12 hours in a workday.

faq.q: Should overtime be on the quote?
faq.a: Yes. Quote the hours the crew will really work, put overtime on its own lines, and state your overtime terms in the notes so the final invoice matches what the client approved.

posts.title: The freelance AV invoice: what to include
posts.description: What to put on an AV freelancer invoice: gig details, line items, overtime, expenses and payment terms, so AV companies pay without questions.
posts.imageAlt: The freelance AV invoice: what to include

faq.q: What should a freelance AV invoice include?
faq.a: Your name and contact details, the AV company and contact you're billing, an invoice number and date, the event, venue, show dates and your position, one line per charge with quantity and rate, the total, and your payment terms and payment method.

faq.q: Should I bill overtime on a separate line?
faq.a: Yes. Put overtime on its own line with the date and hours, and note on the day-rate line how many hours the day rate covers. That way the company can check it against the call times.

faq.q: Do I need to send a W-9 with my invoice?
faq.a: Most US companies ask independent contractors for a Form W-9 before paying them the first time. Sending it with your first invoice to a new company avoids a delay. Ask your accountant about your own tax situation.

faq.q: When should I send the invoice?
faq.a: As soon as the gig wraps, ideally within a day or two. Invoices sent while the show is fresh are easier for the company to match and approve.

posts.description: The structure of a clear AV quote, from event details to labor and terms, and the details that get quotes approved faster.

faq.q: What should an AV quote include?
faq.a: Your company details, client and event details, equipment grouped by category with quantities and rental days, labor lines with hours, delivery and setup, discount, tax and total, deposit and payment terms, and notes such as the cancellation policy.

faq.q: Should labor be separate from equipment on an AV quote?
faq.a: Yes. Separate labor lines with hours make the quote easier to compare and prevent disputes about overtime after the event.

faq.q: How do I handle changes to a quote?
faq.a: Save each change as a new revision instead of overwriting the original. That way you always know which version the client approved.

posts.title: What an AV pull sheet is and how to make one
posts.description: What an AV pull sheet is, what goes on every line, and how to build one from the approved quote so nothing gets left behind.
posts.imageAlt: What an AV pull sheet is and how to make one

faq.q: What is an AV pull sheet?
faq.a: A pull sheet is a checklist of every item to pull from the warehouse, test and load for a job, with quantities, locations and case assignments. It's the crew's version of the quote.

faq.q: What's the difference between a pull sheet and a pack list?
faq.a: The terms overlap, and shops use them differently. Many use pull sheet for the list of gear to take from the shelf, and pack list or load list for what goes in each case or truck. Pick one meaning and stay consistent.

faq.q: Should a pull sheet include spares?
faq.a: Yes. List batteries, cables, adapters and consumables as their own section so they're pulled on purpose, not if there's room.

faq.q: Who should make the pull sheet?
faq.a: Whoever owns the quote should generate it from the approved version. Building it separately is what lets the two drift apart.

posts.title: Day rate or hourly? Pricing AV freelance work
posts.description: Day rate or hourly for AV freelance work? How each works, when to use which, a side-by-side example and what to put in writing.
posts.imageAlt: Day rate or hourly? Pricing AV freelance work

faq.q: Should an AV freelancer charge a day rate or an hourly rate?
faq.a: Use a day rate for full show days and installs with a fixed call, and an hourly rate with a minimum for short or open-ended work. State what the rate covers either way.

faq.q: How do you convert a day rate to an hourly rate?
faq.a: Divide the day rate by the hours it covers. A $600 day covering 10 hours is $60 an hour.

faq.q: What is a half-day rate in AV?
faq.a: A half-day rate is a lower flat price for a short call, often 4 to 5 hours. Many freelancers use it as the minimum call so a short booking still pays fairly.

faq.q: Do I need to write down my rate?
faq.a: Yes. Put the rate, the hours it covers, the minimum call and your overtime start time in the booking email or invoice terms so everyone agrees before the call.

posts.title: Multi-day AV rentals: how to price day 2 and 3
posts.description: Multi day AV rental pricing: how to charge day 2, day 3 and a full week, with a worked example and how to show the rule on your quote.
posts.imageAlt: Multi-day AV rentals: how to price day 2 and 3

faq.q: How do you price day 2 and day 3 of an AV rental?
faq.a: Charge the full rate on day 1, then a set percentage of it on each extra day, often 50% to 75% depending on how fast the gear can be rebooked. Write the percentage on the quote.

faq.q: Should every item get the same multi-day discount?
faq.a: No. Gear that is in constant demand can stay at a flat day rate, while specialty gear that rarely goes out can carry a deeper discount to win the booking. Group your items and set a rule for each group.

faq.q: What is a weekly rate for AV equipment?
faq.a: A weekly rate is a cap on the total for a seven-day rental, written as a multiple of the day rate. Some published schedules use 3.5 times the day rate; yours should reflect how often the item is booked.

posts.title: Spreadsheet vs software for AV quoting
posts.description: When a spreadsheet is enough for AV quotes, where Excel and Google Sheets break down, and how to decide when to switch.
posts.imageAlt: Spreadsheet vs software for AV quoting

faq.q: Is a spreadsheet good enough for AV quoting?
faq.a: For a small number of similar jobs, yes. It stops being good enough when you revise quotes often, calculate crew overtime by hand, or retype quotes into invoices.

faq.q: What are the biggest risks of quoting in Excel or Google Sheets?
faq.a: Stale prices in copied files, formula errors that nobody notices, overtime calculated inconsistently, and lost earlier versions of a quote.

faq.q: Can I fix a spreadsheet instead of switching?
faq.a: Partly. Keep one locked price tab, pull prices with lookup formulas, and save every revision under a clear name. It takes discipline, and it still won't turn the approved quote into an invoice for you.

posts.title: Sales tax on AV rentals and labor: what to check
posts.description: Is AV rental, labor and delivery taxable? The questions to ask your state, plus California's rental guidance as an example. General info, not tax advice.
posts.imageAlt: Sales tax on AV rentals and labor: what to check

faq.q: Do I charge sales tax on AV equipment rentals?
faq.a: It depends on your state and how the rental is structured. Many states tax equipment rentals, but the details differ. Check your state tax agency's guide for rental companies and ask your accountant.

faq.q: Is AV labor taxable?
faq.a: States differ. Some tax certain labor connected to a rental, others do not, and a separately stated charge is often treated differently from a bundled one. Keep labor on its own line and confirm your state's rule.

faq.q: Are delivery and setup fees taxable?
faq.a: Sometimes. In California, for example, delivery in your own vehicle is generally taxable, with exceptions for separately stated charges after the lease starts. Other states have other rules.

faq.q: Where can I find my state's rules?
faq.a: Start with your state's department of revenue or tax agency website, look for guides for rental companies or equipment leasing, and confirm anything unclear with an accountant.
